records.text: Review outreach unanswered
records.speaker: Anonymous Source #14 (Ep bIuvTKlFeGo)

appearances.snippet: We learned that despite repeated outreach attempts, the project team did not receive responses from the following individuals or other representatives of their organizations. This information is included solely to document outreach efforts and to provide transparency regarding the scope of information available to the project team. ... The project team reached out to Brian Harpole, who was identified as the leader of the Integrity Solutions security team working with Turning Point USA to provide executive protection for TPUSA CEO Charlie Kirk. ... The project team attempted to reach Harpole (Brian Harpole) by telephone and certified letter. The certified letter explained the purpose of the outreach and provided the project team contact information. ... The project team did not receive a response. Neither did I, actually. We're going to get more into Dan Flood.

links.title: What led here and what followed

records.notes: As read by Owens, the review documents unanswered telephone and certified-letter outreach to Harpole, giving the institutional-noncooperation narrative a specific review process.

records.text: UVU bad faith rejected
records.speaker: Anonymous Source #14 (Ep bIuvTKlFeGo)

appearances.snippet: It is the opinion right there. It is the opinion of the project team based on our review of all available information that at no time during the events leading up to the assassination of Charlie Kirk or in its aftermath did any employee or agent of UVU act in bad faith or in willful and wanton disregard for the safety of others.

links.title: What led here and what followed

records.notes: The review, as read on the show, concludes no UVU employee or agent acted in bad faith or willful and wanton disregard, while acknowledging safety improvements were needed.

records.text: TPUSA venue choice documented
records.speaker: Anonymous Source #14 (Ep bIuvTKlFeGo)

appearances.snippet: Actually, you know what let's let's go to 2.3. Yeah, let's go to even below that during the August 25th major events teams meeting. ... Macy Crofts, we're going to talk about her more, a senior field representative for Turning Point USA participated at the request of Turning Point USA. ... So again, that's national. Okay. UVU participants raised concerns regarding Turning Point USA's requested location in a large tiered fountain courtyard near the main entrance. ... Concerns included anticipated attendance, potential protest activity, crowd management, and the ability to control access. UVU officials suggested alternative locations such as the Fulton Library, the Quad, or interior locations where access could be more effectively controlled. ... UVU also suggested using the university's ticketing system so anticipated attendance could be tracked and incorporated into the planning. According to meeting participants, Crofts (Macy Crofts) insisted—using the word 'insisted'—on the use of the fountain courtyard location because Charlie Kirk had previously spoken on campus and Turning Point USA was familiar with that location. He also previously spoke at a location with me, and we weren't—we were not in the courtyard. You ... She said that she preferred that TPUSA manage online ticketing through its national office in Phoenix. And when certain major events members expressed reservations, including Robin Ebmeyer, UVU's director of emergency management and safety. ... The committee ultimately allowed the event to proceed in the requested location and allowed Turning Point USA to manage ticketing. Elsewhere, they're going to tell us the reason for that is because they didn't want to violate free speech, essentially, that they're in this Catch-22 situation because you have to allow people to protest.

links.title: What led here and what followed

records.notes: The review, as read by Owens, attributes the courtyard choice and national-office ticketing preference to Crofts despite UVU proposals for alternative locations and university ticketing.

records.text: Drone geography challenged
records.speaker: Anonymous Source #14 (Ep bIuvTKlFeGo)

appearances.snippet: You want to know why it's a lie? Well, the project's team's basic research indicated that drone operations are restricted within a five-mile radius of Provo Airport and Class D airspace, restricted within a five-mile radius of Provo Airport and Class D airspace, just as we reported on this podcast. ... Orem is not within five miles of the Provo Airport airspace, so he lied. He expressed concern that UVUPD did not have a drone available.

records.text: Drone explanation unresolved
records.speaker: Anonymous Source #14 (Ep bIuvTKlFeGo)

appearances.snippet: Without being able to speak directly with Harpole (Brian Harpole), it remains unclear to the project team why during the hours before Charlie Kirk's arrival, Harpole (Brian Harpole)'s team in UVU did not discuss efforts to secure a drone. ... It says that if the team had concerns for the venue location, a drone from the neighboring Orem Police Department could have been requested.

links.title: What led here and what followed

records.notes: The review says it could not determine why Harpole’s team and UVU did not discuss securing a drone without speaking to Harpole, while identifying a possible Orem police drone request.

appearances.snippet: However, if that's what he was concerned about the roofs, then it's unclear why he did not post any members of his team in elevated locations for general security observation purposes.

links.title: What led here and what followed

records.text: Joint planning gaps specified
records.speaker: Anonymous Source #14 (Ep bIuvTKlFeGo)

appearances.snippet: Scroll down a little bit more. Just that top. At the same time, the preparation process revealed several important gaps. ... There was limited time between chief long first learning of the event and the event date. The security assessment process did not result in documented requirements for venue modification. ... The university-controlled ticketing, controlled access, credentialing, screening or additional staffing. UVU did not have reliable access to ticketing or registration data. ... Coordination with TPUSA's security team was very limited and didn't—and did not include a structured pre-event briefing or site walk-through before or on September 10th between Brian Harpole, Dan Flood, and the UVU PD.

links.title: What led here and what followed

records.notes: The review reports limited planning time, undocumented key security controls, unreliable UVU registration data, and no structured pre-event joint briefing or site walk-through.

records.text: UVU resource gaps retained

records.text: Formal credentials absent
records.speaker: Anonymous Source #14 (Ep bIuvTKlFeGo)

appearances.snippet: I do want to point out the bottom of page 1661, because then we learned that Turning Point never actually issued any tickets, which is, by the way, I will say common because they just tell you that you have to register for the event. ... So they did not require tickets at the actual event. Why would they if there's no traffic control? ... They just allowed people to freely register, again, handled entirely by Turning Point USA National and not communicated to the police. But it calls into question. ... The wristbands that were given out. The review states that there was no formal credentialing process for VIPs. It tells us that so who they had somebody from turning point national handing out wristbands to people that were sitting in the section to the right of Charlie (Charlie Kirk). ... learning that there was no ticket verification, there was no credentialing, there was no screening, there was no designated entry and exit points, there were no restricted access areas.

links.title: What led here and what followed

records.notes: The review as conveyed by Owens says event tickets were not required and formal VIP credentialing, ticket verification, screening and restricted entry arrangements were absent.

records.text: EMP tip deemed unreliable
records.speaker: Anonymous Source #14 (Ep bIuvTKlFeGo)

appearances.snippet: So they work with that government bureau when they are dealing with cybersecurity threats. Chief Long (Jeff Long) contacted S-I-A-C by email at approximately 7.30 a.m. on September 10th to share an anonymous tip to UVU. ... you received regarding a potential threat involving an electromagnetic pulse device that a suspect might be using at the event. ... Chief Long (Jeff Long) was seeking to determine whether any threat-related intelligence update was available regarding the tip. Long was advised email was the best method to request information from the Utah SIAC. ... The SIAC responded shortly thereafter to Chief Long (Jeff Long) that it was not a credible threat as it appeared the tipster had provided similar information in the past that was determined to be unreliable. I feel like this is an area that I would like to know more about.

links.title: What led here and what followed

records.notes: The review says Long sought SIAC intelligence about an anonymous EMP-device tip on the event morning and SIAC judged it not credible because the tipster had provided similar unreliable information.
